claims.text: Greatest improvement in diet quality over a 12-year period is associated with lower all-cause mortality according to the Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010 score (pooled HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.97).
Greatest improvement in diet quality over a 12-year period is associated with lower all-cause mortality according to the Alternate Mediterranean Diet score (pooled HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.78-0.91).
Greatest improvement in diet quality over a 12-year period is associated with lower all-cause mortality according to the DASH diet score (pooled HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.84-0.95).
A 20-percentile increase in diet scores across three diet indexes is significantly associated with an 8 to 17% reduction in total mortality.
A 20-percentile increase in diet scores measured by Alternate Healthy Eating Index and Alternate Mediterranean Diet is associated with a 7 to 15% reduction in cardiovascular disease mortality.
Consistently maintaining a high-quality diet over a 12-year period reduces all-cause mortality by 14% when assessed with the Alternate Healthy Eating Index score.
Consistently maintaining a high-quality diet over a 12-year period reduces all-cause mortality by 11% when assessed with the Alternate Mediterranean Diet score.
Consistently maintaining a high-quality diet over a 12-year period reduces all-cause mortality by 9% when assessed with the DASH diet score.

evidence.description: Pooled hazard ratio for all-cause mortality comparing 13-33% improvement vs 0-3% improvement was 0.91 (95% CI, 0.85 to 0.97) using the Alternate Healthy Eating Index score.
Pooled hazard ratio for all-cause mortality comparing 13-33% improvement vs 0-3% improvement was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91) using the Alternate Mediterranean Diet score.
Pooled hazard ratio for all-cause mortality comparing 13-33% improvement vs 0-3% improvement was 0.89 (95% CI, 0.84 to 0.95) using the DASH score.
A 20-percentile increase in diet scores was significantly associated with a reduction in total mortality of 8 to 17% with the use of the three diet indexes.

A 20-percentile increase in diet scores was associated with a 7 to 15% reduction in the risk of death from cardiovascular disease with Alternate Healthy Eating Index and Alternate Mediterranean Diet scores.

Among participants maintaining high-quality diet over 12 years, all-cause mortality risk was lower by 14% (95% CI, 8 to 19) when assessed with Alternate Healthy Eating Index score compared to consistently low scores.

Among participants maintaining high-quality diet over 12 years, all-cause mortality risk was lower by 11% (95% CI, 5 to 18) when assessed with Alternate Mediterranean Diet score compared to consistently low scores.
Among participants maintaining high-quality diet over 12 years, all-cause mortality risk was lower by 9% (95% CI, 2 to 15) when assessed with DASH score compared to consistently low scores.

methodologies.name: Cox proportional-hazards modeling of diet quality change
methodologies.description: Cox proportional-hazards models were used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios for total and cause-specific mortality based on 12-year changes in diet quality scores (Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010, Alternate Mediterranean Diet, DASH).

limitations.text: Few studies have evaluated the relationship between changes in diet quality over time and the risk of death.
